Subject: Marketplace addendum — pass-through carveouts and invoicing

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As we discussed, our procurement team needs the marketplace/reseller addendum updated with two specific items before we can move to signature: 1) explicit pass-through of cloud provider fees (we need the wording to allow automated invoicing of marketplace fees to CloudHarbor instead of Redwood) and 2) an exception to the standard audit notice period for reseller flows (they want a 14-day notice, not 30).

I attached a proposed addendum (CH-Marketplace-Addendum-v2.pdf) with inline suggested language. High level notes:
- Section 2.3: suggested clause to allow marketplace billing flow to be routed through CloudHarbor; they propose a carveout to Redwood's standard reseller liability language.
- Section 5: proposed audit notice change and a confidentiality carve for marketplace invoicing records.

Can your legal/ops team review and confirm whether these are acceptable or if you need counter-language? We are aiming to finish redlines by Monday so our CFO can clear the Order Form.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Best,
Lina Gomez
Head of Partnerships | CloudHarbor

Team — forwarding CloudHarbor's proposed addendum. They want two asks that impact billing and audit terms. Quick context: CloudHarbor will be a marketplace reseller for our hosted offering; they want marketplace fees routed through their billing stack (pass-through) and a shorter audit notice window.

Required: legal redlines for our standard marketplace addendum, and an ops assessment on how pass-through invoicing would affect our billing reconciliation (chargebacks, tax handling).

Please reply with: 1) legal take (acceptable / needs counter / flat no) and specific counter-language if needed, 2) ops note on feasibility and any required instrument changes, 3) whether we can accept a 14-day audit notice and what guardrails we need.

Timeline: CloudHarbor wants redlines by end of Monday (2026-12-14). I know that's tight — if we can't make Monday, propose the earliest feasible date.

Thanks — Marissa

Marissa — quick take after a first pass on their PDF and a sync with Billing Ops: 

Legal (high level):
- Pass-through invoicing: we should avoid language that transfers Redwood's tax and collection obligations to the reseller. Suggested counter: allow marketplace-fee routing but keep Redwood as invoicing provider of record; include explicit indemnity carveouts limited to fees actually paid to cloud provider and supported by receipts.
- Audit notice: 14 days is short. We can accept 14 days only if the scope is tightly limited (e.g., invoices and fee-routing records only, no full SOC/production audits), and the review must be remote with a documented checklist. Suggested language provided in redlines_20261211.docx.

Ops/Billing notes (from sync with Jordan):
- We can implement a pass-through billing flow for marketplace fees but need a mechanical mapping: fast path is to emit an invoice line item with a passthrough tag and push a CSV to CloudHarbor's SFTP weekly. Real-time push would require engineering work and a contract amendment to ETA ~6 weeks.
- Tax/treatment: If CloudHarbor is collecting marketplace fees on their invoices, we need a representation that they will handle VAT/sales tax and provide tax IDs. Otherwise Redwood must remain the VAT-collecting party.

Action items I recommend now:
1) Legal: publish counter-language for Sections 2.3 and 5 that preserves Redwood's tax/collection obligations and limits audit scope. (I'll attach redlines doc)
2) Ops: propose two implementation tiers — (A) short-term weekly CSV export + invoice tagging (no code) and (B) longer-term API/SFTP automation (6-8 weeks). Jordan, please confirm SFTP cadence and any security requirements.

I can send a tracked redline to Lina if you want.

Ben Carter
Director, Partnerships Operations
Redwood Inference
attachments: redlines_20261211.docx

Subject: Re: Marketplace addendum — pass-through carveouts and invoicing

Hi Lina / CloudHarbor legal — thank you for the addendum and for the quick timeline. We reviewed internally and have a proposed set of redlines attached (redlines_20261211.docx). Summary of our counter-proposals below so your team can review quickly: 

1) Pass-through billing: we can support routing marketplace fee lines to CloudHarbor, but Redwood must remain the invoicing entity of record and retain tax collection responsibility unless CloudHarbor provides valid tax IDs and accepts tax collection responsibilities in writing. We added a representation clause and an indemnity narrowly limited to fees paid to third-party cloud providers and evidenced by receipts.

2) Audit window: we can shorten notice to 14 days for marketplace-specific invoicing records only. We limited the audit scope to billing reconciliation documents, restricted to remote access or secure SFTP delivery, and excluded production/operational systems and SOC reports. We also require a mutually agreed checklist and a one-hour remediation period for any data gaps before an escalation.

3) Implementation options: Ben's ops note stands — we can start with a weekly CSV export (no engineering change) and move to an API/SFTP integration (6–8 weeks) if CloudHarbor wants automation. Jordan, will share required SFTP security controls.

Next steps: 
- Lina: please confirm acceptance of the two changes above or propose alternate wording by EOD Tuesday (2026-12-15).
- CloudHarbor Legal: if acceptable, we can exchange DocuSign-ready addenda; I'll initiate once we have final redlines.
- Ops: Jordan / Ben will schedule a short kickoff for the CSV export if CloudHarbor is OK with the interim approach.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quickly.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
